meta.title: Leo's Rainforest Cartoon
meta.textType: dialogue: a short talk with facts

paragraphs: On Thursday, the rain was very heavy, so the Explorers stayed indoors in the library. Leo stood next to a big cartoon poster of a green frog. He spent a week on the cartoon. Mia, May, and Lily sat in the front row. The frog wore red trainers and held a small wallet. "Today I will talk about the rainforest," said Leo. "But first, a joke." "Why does this frog wear trainers?" "Because the forest floor is wet!"

Mia laughed, and Teacher Kim smiled. "Now the first fact," said Leo. "A rainforest gets more than two hundred and fifty centimeters of rain every year." "That is why it is so green." "A rainforest has four layers." "The top layer has very tall trees, up to sixty meters." "The second layer is like a green roof, and many birds live there." Leo showed a picture of a hornbill with a big yellow beak.

"The third layer is for small trees," said Leo. "The fourth layer is the ground, and it is dark and wet." "Plants on the ground have very big leaves, because only a little light comes down." "That is where my frog lives, and that is why he needs trainers." "What is the wallet for?" asked May. "The frog wants to buy a dry house," said Leo. "But there are no shops in the rainforest, so the wallet is empty." Everybody laughed again.

"Now let's discuss," said Teacher Kim. "Why are rainforests important?" "Many animals live there," said Mia. "If the trees disappear, the animals will lose their homes." "Trees also make the air clean," said Lily. "There are rainforests in the south of Thailand, too," said May. "I want to visit one with my family."

Leo gave his cartoon poster to Teacher Kim. "Thank you," she said. "I will put it on the library wall." "Your talk had a joke and many good facts." Lily wrote the facts in her notebook for the blog post. Outside the window, the rain stopped, and the sun came out. Leo smiled and said, "Now the frog can take off his trainers."
